tools.lede: The registry is the only source of tools an agent can see. What an agent may do with one is the classification below, the grants the broker mints, and the switches that can deny it at any level.

tabs.label: Tools sections
tabs.switchesOnAtLeast: {count, plural, one {# or more on} other {# or more on}}

registry.title: Tool versions
registry.lead: Access reaches the version. A server shipping a new version does not silently widen a belt.
registry.categoriesNote: These tags and counts are this page of the registry. A tag carried only by a version on a later page appears once you reach that page.
registry.categoriesDeclaredNote: These chips and the Category column show the tags recorded with a version's classification. A version can also carry tags declared where it was published, and both the filter and a class kill switch match those too — so a tag can select a version whose row shows none, and the Financial column can confirm a money tag but never rule one out.
registry.categoriesFilteredNote: While a tag is selected, these chips count only the versions matching it: they are the tags carried alongside that one, not the registry's. Clear the filter to see the rest.
registry.emptyCategory: No tool version on this page carries that tag.
registry.gateNote: The gate shown is today’s, in the recorded order: the version’s own kill switch, then its server’s, then a class switch matching its consequence tags.

empty.title: No tool version is registered
empty.body: Until a server is imported, no agent in this workspace has a belt, and every call by name is unknown_tool. Import a registered MCP server to pull its tools/list, version it, and store its schema.

classify.lead: Classification describes the tool and decides nothing by itself: a class kill switch matches a version by its consequence tags at call time, and the approval rules are written against it. Reclassifying is a governed action and is recorded in Audit.
classify.tagsHint: Space- or comma-separated, snake_case. The starter set is moves_money, destroys_data, alters_production, communicates_externally, changes_access, changes_entitlement; a tag of your own that fits the pattern is accepted.
classify.dataClassesHint: One per line. A data class is free text up to 64 characters, so it may contain spaces: customer financial data is one class, not three.
classify.reasonHint: Recorded on the version. The security event carries the actor and the capability, not the reason.
classify.denied: Reclassifying a tool version needs an organization Owner or Admin.

import.open: Import tools from an MCP server
import.title: Import tools from an MCP server
import.body: Pulls the registered server’s pinned tools/list into this workspace’s registry: one immutable version per changed manifest. Re-importing an unchanged server changes nothing.
import.toolsHint: Space- or comma-separated names. Leave it blank to import every pinned tool the server has.
import.done: {published, plural, =0 {No new version} one {# new version} other {# new versions}} · {unchanged, plural, =0 {nothing unchanged} one {# already registered} other {# already registered}}.
import.serverPickHint: Every server registered in this workspace. Registering one is below the registry.
import.serverFallbackHint: The server roster could not be read, so the server is named by its id.
import.serverNone: No server is registered yet, so there is nothing to import from.

connections.title: Credential grants
connections.lead: Every credential the broker put to use for a tool server on behalf of a run, with the connection it drew on and how far it was narrowed. No agent holds any of these; the agent sees the result, never the credential.
connections.brokerNote: For each dispatched call the broker mints the narrowest credential the provider allows — a token exchange, a session policy, a restricted key, or the stored credential used server-side for that call only.
connections.notCarriedNote: The record carries the server the credential was presented to, not the tool version or the agent that asked for it, so neither is shown here rather than guessed.

empty.title: No credential has been put to use
empty.body: A grant is recorded the first time a governed run reaches a tool server through a stored connection.

list.title: Connections
list.lead: Every stored connection this workspace can reach a tool server through. A connection holds the credential; a grant below is one use of it.

empty.title: No connection is stored
empty.body: Until a connection is added, no run in this workspace can reach a tool server that needs a credential.

list.notCarriedNote: Owner, Reviewed and Next review have no field on the connection record, so they are shown as not recorded rather than guessed.
list.credentialNote: The stored credential is never read back to this page. The broker mints a narrowed credential per call and records the grant below.
list.denied: Reading this connection needs a role this workspace has not given you.
list.failed: This connection could not be read: {code}.

add.title: Add a connection
add.body: Stores a credential for one connector and names it. The credential is encrypted before it reaches a row, and nothing reads it back to this page.
add.connectorHint: The connector type slug, such as github or stripe. A slug this deployment has no connector for is refused.
add.displayNameHint: What this connection is called in the ledger and on a grant. Up to 255 characters.
add.schemeHint: Which credential the connector authenticates with. Another scheme is created over the API until a form can collect it safely.
add.deliveryHint: Leave it blank to keep the connector's own default.
add.secretNote: The credential is sent once and is not shown again. Nothing here logs it and no answer carries it back.
add.done: {name} is stored as {id}. Its status is pending setup: the credential is held and nothing has drawn on it yet.

switches.title: Deny is available at every level
switches.lead: A flip takes effect at the next call boundary by bumping the deny generation, so every live run token is re-checked at its next call. Runs in flight are not killed; their next call fails closed and the frame names the switch and the reason.
switches.generation: Deny generation: {org} organization-wide, {workspace} in this workspace.
switches.classHeading: Class switches · organization-wide, in one action
switches.empty: No kill switch has ever been flipped in this workspace. Flip one to record the first.
switches.truncated: This board shows the {limit} newest switches and the record holds more, so the count on the tab is a floor. An older switch that is still denying is not on this page; flip it through the API or MCP, which name a switch by its target rather than by a page.
switches.takesEffect: at the next call boundary, through deny generation {generation}

blastRadius.class: Every tool version carrying this consequence tag, across the organization — including one imported tomorrow.
blastRadius.org: Every agent in every workspace of this organization.
blastRadius.tool_server: Every tool version this server has published.
blastRadius.tool_version: This version only. Another version of the same tool is untouched.
blastRadius.connection: This connection, and every credential grant behind it: live grants are revoked with the flip.
blastRadius.operator: Every agent this operator is accountable for.

targetHint.class: The consequence tag every stopped tool carries, such as moves_money.
targetHint.operator: Every agent this member is accountable for is denied.

dialog.targetOperatorEmpty: No org members to choose from.
dialog.blastBody: Every affected call is denied at its next boundary. Nothing in flight is killed, and nothing is destroyed — you can clear this switch at any time.
dialog.restoreBody: Denied calls resume at the next boundary. Nothing that was denied while the switch was on is retried.
dialog.classNote: A class switch names no server and no agent: it matches a tool version by its declared consequence tags, so a tool imported tomorrow carrying this tag is denied the moment it enters the registry.
dialog.connectionNote: A connection switch also revokes every credential grant that drew on it.
dialog.reason: Reason — recorded on every denied call
dialog.takesEffectValueIfChanged: next call boundary · deny generation {from} → {to}, if this flip changes the switch. A target already denied at this level is left as it is, and nothing advances.
dialog.recordedAsValue: a security event, with who, when and why
dialog.unchanged: Nothing changed: the switch was already that way, so no deny generation advanced and nothing new was recorded.

switches.noNames: A flip records the public id of whoever made it, the same usr_… id list_members and the audit log print. The record carries no display name, so this page prints the id rather than guessing at a person.

denied.title: You cannot see the tool registry
denied.body: The roles you hold on this organization do not include the tool read on this workspace. An owner can grant it, and the grant is itself a governed action in the audit record.
denied.decidedBy: Decided by: the workspace’s decision rules — deny wins over every allow.

pending.title: Access to this workspace’s tools is waiting for approval

error.title: Tools could not be loaded
error.body: Nothing was changed. Runs kept recording while this page was down: frames are written by the gateway, not by the operator console.

failure.orgRoleRequired: This needs an organization Owner or Admin. Nothing was changed.
failure.noPrincipal: This session carries no person to record the action against. Nothing was changed.
failure.serverNotFound: No registered tool server has that id in this workspace.
failure.versionNotFound: No tool version has that id in this workspace.
failure.killSwitchOn: A kill switch names this target, so it cannot be changed until the switch is cleared.
failure.invalid: Check the values above and try again.
failure.pendingApproval: This is waiting for approval. Access request {accessRequestId}.
failure.unavailable: Could not be recorded ({code}). Nothing was changed.
failure.consequenceRoleRequired: Saving this rule needs an organization Owner or Admin who also holds the role accountable for every consequence its tools carry. Nothing was changed.
failure.noRoleCoversAllTags: No single organization role is accountable for every consequence these tools carry together. Split the rule by tool. Nothing was changed.
failure.ruleIdTaken: A rule with that id already exists. Pick another id, or edit that rule. Nothing was changed.
failure.ruleChanged: Someone else changed this rule set while this dialog was open, so nothing was written. Reload the tab to see the rules as they are now, then make the change again.
failure.ruleNotFound: That rule is no longer in this workspace’s rule set. Reload the tab to see the rules as they are now.
failure.noToolMatches: A tool pattern matches no declared tool in this workspace. Nothing was changed.
failure.ruleNotGated: A tool pattern matches a tool that Oxagen does not route through the decision rules, so a rule over it would never be enforced. Nothing was changed.
failure.measureNotDeclared: A condition names a measure that a matched tool does not declare. Nothing was changed.
failure.measureWrongType: A condition names a measure of the wrong kind: a ceiling needs an amount or a count, and an allow list needs a text measure. Nothing was changed.
failure.tooManyConsequences: The rule’s tools carry more than 64 distinct consequences. Narrow its tool patterns. Nothing was changed.

mandates.title: Mandates ledger
mandates.lead: The mandates this workspace has recorded — granted, requested, expired and revoked — with what each has settled, what calls in flight hold, and what is left. A mandate is the only thing that lets an agent carry a consequence, and every draw on it reserves, then settles or releases.
mandates.empty: This workspace has recorded no mandate: none granted, and none requested.
mandates.emptyDetail: A call that carries a consequence tag with no mandate is denied before dispatch, whether or not the tool is on the agent's belt.
mandates.truncated: The newest {shown} mandates. This workspace has recorded at least that many, and older ones are not listed here.
mandates.partial: You see the mandates of the agents you created and any mandate you requested yourself. This ledger is not every mandate this workspace has recorded.
mandates.emptyListed: No mandate is listed here. The ledger above is not complete, so that is not a statement that the workspace has recorded none.
mandates.emptyListedDetail: An org Owner, Admin, Billing or Compliance reader sees every mandate this workspace has recorded. This ledger is written for that office.

grant.title: Grant a mandate
grant.body: The mandate is active from the first day you pick. It lets one agent carry the consequences you name, within the limits below, until the last day. Your role is recorded with the grant.
grant.bodyRequest: The request is prefilled. What you submit replaces it and becomes active, and your role is recorded with the grant.
grant.notCarried: This request holds more than this form can carry: a money limit, a second limit, target rule or threshold, a calls limit that is not a daily total, or a tool pattern or target pattern with a comma in it. Granting it here would drop or split that part and grant more than was asked, so it cannot be granted here. Grant it over the API or MCP with grant_mandate.
grant.agentsPartial: The first page of this workspace's agents. An agent not listed here can be granted a mandate over the API or MCP.
grant.agentsUnavailable: The workspace's agents could not be read, so there is no agent to pick. Reload the page to try again.
grant.agentsEmpty: This workspace has no agent that can hold a mandate. A retired agent cannot.
grant.consequenceOther: Others the tools declare, separated by commas
grant.consequenceTagsHint: Name every consequence the covered tools declare. A mandate covers a tool only when it names all of them. Your org role has to be accountable for every consequence you name.
grant.toolsHint: Patterns over slug@version, separated by commas. Each has to match a declared tool. Everything else is denied.
grant.limitsHint: Name a measure limit, a calls cap, or both. Every figure is whole units and is recorded exactly as typed.
grant.measureHint: The name the tool version declares the figure under. It cannot be “calls”: the calls field sets that limit.
grant.unitHint: What the measure counts, in the unit the tool version declares. Not a currency code: a money limit is granted over the API or MCP.
grant.perPeriodHint: Name a per-call limit, a per-period limit, or both.
grant.targetsHint: Optional. Which targets one measure may be drawn against, such as a payee or a recipient. Leave these blank for no rule.
grant.approvalHint: Optional. When a person answers a call this mandate would otherwise allow. Leave these blank and no call waits for a person.
grant.alwaysHumanForHint: Consequences for which a person answers every call, separated by commas.
grant.humanAboveValueHint: Whole units of that measure, recorded exactly as typed. A call above it waits for a person.
grant.approversHint: role:Owner, role:Admin, role:Billing, role:Compliance, or user:usr_…, separated by commas. Blank leaves the answer to the roles accountable for the consequence.
grant.purposeHint: Written for the office that reads the ledger.
grant.validToHint: A mandate expires. There is no unbounded option.

fields.targetMeasure: Measure the target is read from
fields.humanAboveMeasure: Ask a person above, on measure

failure.orgRoleRequired: Your org role is not accountable for every consequence this mandate names. Nothing was granted.
failure.noRoleCoversAllTags: No single org role is accountable for every consequence named here, so nobody can grant them together. Grant them as separate mandates. Nothing was granted.
failure.noPrincipal: This session carries no person to record the grant against. Nothing was granted.
failure.agentNotFound: That agent is not recorded in this workspace. Nothing was granted.
failure.agentHasNoPrincipal: That agent has no identity a mandate can bind to. Nothing was granted.
failure.mandateNotFound: That request is not recorded in this workspace. Nothing was granted.
failure.notADraft: That request was granted or declined by someone else first. Nothing was granted.
failure.noToolMatches: A tool pattern matches no declared tool that carries a consequence. Nothing was granted.
failure.measureNotDeclared: A tool this mandate covers declares no such measure, so a limit or a target on it could never be read from a call. Nothing was granted.
failure.measureUnitMismatch: A tool this mandate covers declares that measure in another unit. Nothing was granted.
failure.measureKindConflict: Two tools this mandate covers declare that measure differently, one as an amount and one as a count, so there is no single figure to enforce. Narrow the tool patterns. Nothing was granted.
failure.agentRetired: That agent is retired. A retired agent cannot draw on new authority. Nothing was granted.
failure.timeZoneUnavailable: Your time zone could not be read, and the days you picked mean a different instant in each zone. Nothing was granted. Try again.
failure.timeZoneUnsupported: Your saved time zone is not one this server can read, so the days you picked cannot be placed in it. Pick a time zone again in your account settings. Nothing was granted.
failure.refused: The grant was refused: {code}. Nothing was granted.
failure.invalidField: Check the field “{field}”. Nothing was granted.
failure.invalid: Something in the form is not a value a grant accepts. Nothing was granted.
failure.pendingApproval: The grant is waiting for approval. Access request {accessRequestId}.
failure.unavailable: The grant could not be answered: {code}. Nothing was granted.

autoApprovals.title: Auto-approval rules
autoApprovals.lead: A call the policy sends to a person skips them when a rule here covers it and every condition holds. The receipt names the rule as the approver, so it says plainly that no person looked.
autoApprovals.floors: No rule releases a call with tainted input, a call to a critical or irreversible tool, or a call to an undeclared tool. Those floors are code, not configuration.
autoApprovals.counted: Released and held count the approval rows of the last {days} days that name each rule.
autoApprovals.writtenUnattributed: Last written {at}, by no recorded person
autoApprovals.unstamped: Releases nothing until it is saved again: the record does not say which consequences it was checked against.

empty.title: No auto-approval rules yet
empty.body: Every call the policy sends to a person waits for one. Create a rule to let a call that meets its conditions skip the queue.

released.title: Auto-approved, {days} days
released.basis: Calls a rule released with no person

held.title: Sent to a person, {days} days
held.basis: Calls that reached a person with a rule read beside them

requires.standing: A person approved the same call in the last {minutes} minutes

editor.idHint: Lowercase letters, digits, dots, dashes, and underscores. Receipts cite the rule by this id, so it cannot change later.
editor.name: Name
editor.toolsHint: One pattern per line, over slug@version or the bare slug, such as stripe__create_payment@*.
editor.maxMeasuresHint: One measure per line, as measure = value. Micros for a currency, whole units for a count.
editor.allowTargetsHint: One measure per line, as measure = pattern, pattern.
editor.standingMinutesHint: Leave blank for none. A person’s approval of the same call re-applies inside this window.
editor.timezoneHint: An IANA name, such as Europe/London.
editor.checks: Saving checks that every pattern matches a declared tool, that each measure is declared by those tools, and that you hold the role accountable for their consequences.
editor.notCarried: This rule holds a tool pattern with a line break or an allow-list pattern with a comma, which these fields would split into more than one pattern. Saving it here would widen the rule, so it cannot be saved here. Edit it over the API or MCP with set_approval_rules. It can still be switched off or deleted.

unreadable.maxMeasures: Each ceiling line needs a measure, an equals sign, and a value, and names each measure once.
unreadable.allowTargets: Each allow-list line needs a measure, an equals sign, and at least one pattern, and names each measure once.

delete.title: Delete this rule
delete.body: Deleting removes {name} from the rule set. Calls it would have released go to a person.
delete.keep: Switching it off instead keeps its id, so its counters and every receipt that cites {citation} stay readable.

servers.title: Tool servers
servers.lead: The MCP servers registered in this workspace. Importing takes a server's pinned tools into the registry above; the server row is what a tool server kill switch names.

empty.title: No server is registered
empty.body: Registering a server health checks its endpoint and records the tools it pins. Nothing reaches the registry until those tools are imported.

servers.unknownNote: A server installed by a plugin is written with the SSE transport and no health check, so its health reads as not checked until one runs.

register.title: Register an MCP server
register.body: Health checks the endpoint, encrypts any auth config and records the tools the server pins. Importing those tools into the registry is the next step.
register.name: Name
register.transportHint: Register an HTTP endpoint. SSE servers are installed through plugins.
register.endpointHint: An address reachable from the public internet. One that resolves inside this deployment is refused, because the health check carries the auth config to it.
register.authConfigHint: One name = value per line: the bearer token, or the header and its value. It is encrypted before storage and is not shown again.
register.done: {name} is registered as {id}, {health}, with {tools, plural, =0 {no pinned tool} one {# pinned tool} other {# pinned tools}}.
register.stdioNote: A stdio server is not probed from here, so it is recorded as not health checked and pins no tool until one is discovered.
